transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called this review round to go through the proposed receivables sale to the bankruptcy-remote funding vehicle. We have a preliminary proposal with an eligible receivables balance of $8.5 million and a target closing date of June 30, 2026. Before I make my approval decision, I need legal and treasury to walk me through your material findings and any required closing controls. Let's start with legal — what are you seeing on your end?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Maya, I have a material finding from my review of the customer contracts this afternoon. The KITE and NORTHSTAR agreements both prohibit assignment without consent. If we exclude those invoices, the eligible receivables balance drops from $8.5 million to exactly $7.2 million. Additionally, the closing file must include a signed assignment-consent package for both KITE and NORTHSTAR customers before we can proceed. I haven't uploaded this review to the transaction folder yet, but I'll do so promptly.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Maya, I have treasury's material findings from the arranger's funding memo I received this morning. The memo confirms an 85% advance rate and a 5% cash reserve on the $7.2 million eligible pool — which aligns with Jonas's adjusted balance after excluding KITE and NORTHSTAR. The net cash proceeds come to exactly $5,760,000. Treasury requires that the 5% cash reserve be held in a segregated account through the first reporting date as a closing control. I have not yet circulated this memo to the sign-off group, but I'm disclosing it now so everyone has the full picture.
transcript.speaker: A3
